name: Autodesk AutoCAD
description: AutoCAD is Autodesk's general-purpose 2D drafting and 3D modelling application and the de facto interchange standard for technical drawings through its DWG and DXF file formats. Work happens in model space, where geometry is drawn at full scale, and on one or more paper-space layouts that hold title blocks, scaled viewports and plot settings. Objects carry properties inherited from layers (colour, linetype, lineweight, transparency, plot style) and are placed with the aid of object snaps, polar and object-snap tracking, dynamic input and grips. On top of the drawing primitives sit blocks with attributes, dynamic blocks, external references, annotative text and dimensions that scale themselves to the viewport, tables linked to spreadsheets, and a full 3D solid, surface and mesh modelling toolset with visual styles and rendering. Everything is reachable from the command line, which is why AutoCAD automates so well: commands can be typed, scripted, recorded, or driven from AutoLISP, VBA, COM/ActiveX, the managed .NET API or ObjectARX in C++.

automation.summary: AutoCAD exposes the same functionality through several layers. (1) The command line itself: every command can be typed, and a plain-text script file (.scr) is just a list of command input, one response per line, replayed with the SCRIPT command or the /b command-line switch. (2) AutoCAD Core Console (accoreconsole.exe) runs that script against a drawing with no user interface at all, which is the supported way to batch-process thousands of DWGs; its switches are /i for the input drawing, /s for the script, /l for the language pack and /isolate to copy the user registry key so system-variable changes do not leak into the interactive product. (3) AutoLISP and Visual LISP: an interpreted Lisp embedded in the product, loaded from .lsp/.fas/.vlx files, able to call commands with (command ...), build entities directly with (entmake), select with (ssget) and reach the ActiveX object model through the vla-*/vlax-* functions after (vl-load-com). (4) COM/ActiveX automation from any Windows language via the AutoCAD.Application ProgID, driving Documents, ModelSpace, Blocks, Layers, Layouts, SelectionSets and Utility. (5) The managed .NET API (ObjectARX for .NET), loaded in-process with NETLOAD, which is the modern choice for serious add-ins and the only API the Core Console and Design Automation service run. (6) ObjectARX in C++ for maximum performance. (7) Autodesk Platform Services Design Automation for AutoCAD, which runs the Core Console with a custom bundle in the cloud as activities and work items. Python reaches AutoCAD only indirectly, through COM (pywin32 or the pyautocad wrapper).

cli.description: Run a script against a drawing with no graphical interface. This is the headless batch engine: it loads the DWG, replays every line of the script as command-line input, and exits. /i gives the input drawing, /s the script file and /l the language pack. Without /i the console opens an empty drawing based on the default template.

Same as above but first copies the user registry product root key so any system-variable or profile change the script makes stays inside that Core Console instance and does not affect the interactive AutoCAD session. Essential when a batch script sets things like FILEDIA, PLOTROTMODE or measurement units.
Select which vertical product's registry settings and command set to load (ACAD, ACADM for Mechanical, ACADE for Electrical, and so on) when several AutoCAD verticals share a machine.

Start the full AutoCAD interface and immediately run a script. Unlike the Core Console this shows the UI and needs a licence seat, but it can do things the console cannot, such as plotting to a system printer through the display subsystem.
Start a new drawing from a named template with no splash screen, using a specific user profile, and run a script. /p loads a profile (.arg), /t a template, /nologo suppresses the startup screen.

Load an ObjectARX/DBX application at startup (/ld), append folders to the support file search path for the session (/s), set the starting workspace (/w) and restore a named view once the drawing opens (/v).
Publish a drawing set in the background from a saved Drawing Set Description file produced by the PUBLISH command, without opening the drawings interactively.

Script playback from inside a running session: SCRIPT runs a .scr file, RSCRIPT repeats the current one (used for looping demos and slide shows), DELAY pauses for a number of milliseconds and RESUME continues a script that was interrupted by Esc or an error.

apis.name: Script files (.scr)
apis.description: The simplest automation layer: a plain text file where each line is typed at the command prompt exactly as a user would type it, a blank line acts as Enter (so trailing blank lines matter), and a space is a separator. Prefix commands with a hyphen to reach the command-line version of a dialog command (-INSERT, -LAYER, -PURGE) and with an underscore to force the English command name in localised installations; combine both as -_LAYER. Always set FILEDIA 0 and ATTDIA 0 first so no dialog interrupts playback. Scripts cannot branch or loop, which is why anything conditional belongs in LISP or .NET called from the script.
apis.example:
FILEDIA 0
ATTDIA 0
_-PURGE _All * _N
_AUDIT _Y
_ZOOM _E
_-LAYER _S 0 
_QSAVE
_-PLOT _Y Model "DWG To PDF.pc3" "ANSI full bleed D (34.00 x 22.00 Inches)" _I _L _N _E _F _C _Y monochrome.ctb _Y _N _N _Y

apis.name: AutoLISP / Visual LISP
apis.description: An interpreted dialect of Lisp built into AutoCAD, loaded with APPLOAD or (load "file.lsp") and compiled to .fas/.vlx with the Visual LISP IDE. It can call commands with (command ...) or the safer (command-s ...)/(vl-cmdf ...), read and write system variables with getvar/setvar, build selection sets with (ssget), and create or edit entities directly through DXF-coded association lists with entmake, entget, entmod and entdel. (vl-load-com) unlocks the Visual LISP ActiveX layer (vla-*, vlax-*), giving object-oriented access to the same COM model that external languages use. A function named (defun c:NAME ...) becomes a new AutoCAD command.
apis.example:
(vl-load-com)
(defun c:GRIDLINES ( / n p0 acadObj doc ms pt1 pt2)
  (setq doc (vla-get-ActiveDocument (vlax-get-acad-object))
        ms  (vla-get-ModelSpace doc))
  (setq p0 (getpoint "\nStart point: "))
  (setq n (getint "\nNumber of gridlines: "))
  (repeat n
    (setq pt1 (vlax-3d-point p0)
          pt2 (vlax-3d-point (polar p0 (/ pi 2) 5000.0)))
    (vla-AddLine ms pt1 pt2)
    (setq p0 (polar p0 0.0 6000.0)))
  (princ))

apis.name: COM / ActiveX Automation
apis.description: AutoCAD registers the AutoCAD.Application ProgID, so any COM-capable language (VBA, VBScript, C#, VB.NET, Python via pywin32 or pyautocad) can drive a running or newly launched session out of process. The object model is Application > Documents > Document > ModelSpace/PaperSpace/Blocks/Layers/Layouts, with Add* factory methods (AddLine, AddCircle, AddText, AddLightWeightPolyline, AddDimAligned, InsertBlock), a Utility object for interactive input, SelectionSets for picking existing geometry, and SendCommand/PostCommand for anything without a direct method. Out-of-process COM is convenient but slow for bulk work; prefer .NET in-process for large operations.
apis.example:
import win32com.client
acad = win32com.client.Dispatch("AutoCAD.Application")
acad.Visible = True
doc = acad.Documents.Add()
ms = doc.ModelSpace

def pt(x, y, z=0.0):
    import array
    return array.array('d', [x, y, z])

ms.AddLine(pt(0, 0), pt(100, 0))
ms.AddCircle(pt(50, 50), 25.0)
ms.AddText("PLATE 12mm", pt(0, -20), 5.0)
doc.SetVariable("CLAYER", "0")
doc.Application.ZoomExtents()
doc.SaveAs(r"C:\out\plate.dwg")

apis.name: .NET API (managed ObjectARX)
apis.description: The modern in-process API, referenced through accoremgd.dll, acdbmgd.dll and acmgd.dll and loaded at run time with NETLOAD. Code marked with [CommandMethod] becomes an AutoCAD command and [LispFunction] becomes an AutoLISP function. Work is done inside a transaction: open the Database, start a Transaction, open the BlockTable and BlockTableRecord, add or modify DBObjects, then Commit. The Editor object handles prompts (GetPoint, GetSelection, WriteMessage). This is the only API available inside the Core Console and Design Automation, so batch add-ins must be written here rather than in LISP or COM.

apis.name: ObjectARX (C++)
apis.description: The native C++ SDK that the whole application is built on. An ARX module is a DLL with acrxEntryPoint handling load/unload messages, registering commands with acedRegCmds, prompting through acedGetPoint/acedGetString and creating geometry with AcDbLine, AcDbCircle, AcDbBlockTableRecord and friends. It gives the deepest access (custom object classes, reactors, overrules, custom entity graphics) and the best performance, at the cost of having to be recompiled for each AutoCAD release family.

apis.name: Autodesk Platform Services Design Automation for AutoCAD
apis.description: A cloud service that runs AutoCAD Core Console on Autodesk's infrastructure with no local installation. You upload an AppBundle (a .NET plug-in packaged with a PackageContents.xml), define an Activity that describes the command line and the input/output parameters, then POST WorkItems that reference input DWG URLs and receive output URLs back. Useful for server-side DWG generation, extraction and conversion at scale; the same bundle can be tested locally with accoreconsole.exe before upload.

apis.name: Action Recorder and CUI macros
apis.description: Two no-code automation routes. The Action Recorder (ACTRECORD / ACTSTOP) records command input into an .actm action macro that can be replayed with ACTPLAY or ACTMANAGER, with ACTUSERINPUT inserted where the user should supply a value. CUI command macros are the strings behind ribbon, toolbar and menu buttons, written in the Customize User Interface editor: ^C^C cancels any running command, an underscore forces the English name, a hyphen picks the command-line variant, a backslash pauses for user input and a semicolon is Enter.
apis.example:
; CUI macro: draw a 100x50 rectangle at a picked point on layer DIM
^C^C_-LAYER;_M;DIM;;_RECTANG;\@100,50

; Action macro workflow
ACTRECORD
  ZOOM  E
  -PURGE  All  *  N
ACTSTOP

file_formats.description: The native AutoCAD drawing database, holding model and paper space geometry, layers, blocks, styles, layouts, plot settings and object data. Saved with QSAVE/SAVEAS, checked with AUDIT and RECOVER, and down-saved to older releases with SAVEAS or DWGCONVERT.

Drawing Interchange Format, the documented ASCII (or binary) representation of the same database used for exchange with other CAD systems. Written with SAVEAS or DXFOUT and read with DXFIN or OPEN; the group codes it defines are also the codes AutoLISP entget/entmake use.

Drawing template: a DWG saved with standard layers, styles, layouts and title blocks, used by NEW and by the /t command-line switch. The default template is controlled by the QNEW settings in OPTIONS.

Drawing standards file listing approved layers, linetypes, text styles and dimension styles. Associated with a drawing through STANDARDS and checked with CHECKSTANDARDS or the batch standards checker.

Script file: plain text command input replayed by the SCRIPT command, the /b switch or accoreconsole /s. Blank lines are Enter, and no dialog may appear, so FILEDIA/ATTDIA are normally set to 0 first.

AutoLISP source, a compiled Visual LISP FAS module and a VLX application package. Loaded with APPLOAD, (load ...) or automatically from acad.lsp/acaddoc.lsp; SECURELOAD and TRUSTEDPATHS control which folders are allowed to load executable code.
VBA project, managed .NET assembly and native ObjectARX module. Loaded with VBALOAD/VBARUN, NETLOAD and APPLOAD/ARX respectively.
Colour-dependent and named plot style tables that map screen colours or named styles to pen width, screening and dithering at plot time. Selected in PAGESETUP/PLOT and edited with STYLESMANAGER.
Plotter configuration file and plotter model parameter file, created by PLOTTERMANAGER. A .pc3 such as "DWG To PDF.pc3" is what a script names when plotting without a system printer dialog.
Hatch pattern definitions, linetype definitions, compiled shape/font files and TrueType fonts. HPNAME, LINETYPE and STYLE reference them, and they must be on the support file search path to resolve.

Customization file holding ribbon tabs, toolbars, menus, workspaces, keyboard shortcuts and command macros, edited with CUI and loaded with CUILOAD. A matching .mnl file holds the AutoLISP that its macros call.
Design Web Format and PDF output. Created with PLOT, PUBLISH, EXPORTDWF or EXPORTPDF, attached back into a drawing as underlays with DWFATTACH/PDFATTACH, and converted to geometry with PDFIMPORT.
Sheet set data file used by the Sheet Set Manager (SHEETSET) to organise layouts from many drawings into a publishable set with shared properties and fields.
Action macro recorded by the Action Recorder (ACTRECORD/ACTSTOP), replayed with ACTPLAY and managed with ACTMANAGER.
Program parameters file (acad.pgp) defining command aliases such as L for LINE, C for CIRCLE, CO for COPY, TR for TRIM and external command definitions. Reloaded in session with REINIT.
Automatic backup copy, autosave file (SAVETIME interval) and the lock files written while a drawing is open. DRAWINGRECOVERY lists recoverable .sv$ files after a crash.
